messages:
Jules: heads up — saw a few console sessions where dashboard quota graphs are attributing tokens to the wrong org id. happens intermittently, ~5 requests/day. anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
Maria: can you paste one of the raw events/log lines? curious if it's a client->gateway issue or console side prefetch/cache.
Jules: pasted below (sanitized) — noticed X-Org and tenant headers mismatch in the same request:
```
INFO route_req id=abcd123 path=/api/console/render user=u-42 X-Org=org-9 X-Forwarded-For=... cookie=rb_session=...
prefetch_key=route_prefetch::user:u-42:cookie:rb_session
cached_meta={"org":"org-4","quota_window":"2026-03-17T10:00:00Z"}
```
Maria: whoa — cache shows org-4 but request header is org-9. that smells like prefetch cache key omitting the org.
Sam: prefetch layer currently keys on user+cookie only. historically that was fine because we assumed cookie -> org stable, but with rapid org-switching UX we saw cookie reuse.
Lee: confirmed — gateway doesn't tag the prefetch key with X-Org when prefetching on behalf of console. it uses session id only. negative: quick and nasty root cause.
Ana: telemetry question — are we sure billing/quotas were affected or just UI attribution? can we find a customer report?
Jules: found two customers flagged by billing who saw spikes. quota meter backfills look at console-side telemetry so could be double-counting.
Devon: what about fixing at console vs gateway? If gateway changes cache key, it'll be safer for all clients. console-only fix would be narrower but faster.
Sam: gateway change is nontrivial — touches prefetch handshake, might need migration for older sidecars. also rollout risk given large traffic surface.
Maria: alternate mitigation: make console include org in prefetch request and also namespace the cache key locally (console-prefetch:{org}:{session}). that reduces blast radius and is quick.
Lee: downside — console change leaves other clients vulnerable (mobile, integrations) still prefetching without org. but short term ok.
qa-bot: repro checklist suggested:
1) create two orgs, same user in both (impersonation flow)
2) rapid org switch in UI (~5 sec)
3) hit dashboard -> observe prefetched cache entry keeps prior org
4) assert quota attribution mismatch in telemetry
Sam: thanks. I'll add an e2e that simulates fast org-switching and asserts cache key includes org.
Ana: also add a metric org_mismatch_count and a smoke alert if > 1/min across prod zones. want to detect regressions during rollout.
Devon: low risk quick fix plan:
- add org namespace to console prefetch key (small PR)
- add unit + e2e test (Sam)
- add telemetry metric and dashboards (Ana)
- canary deploy to 10% (Jules)
- meanwhile open gateway ticket for authoritative fix (Lee)
Maria: for the console PR, include a feature flag (prefetch.use_org_namespace) so we can flip back if something unexpected happens. also update rollout UX doc for sticky-switch behavior.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary release scheduled for 1711116000 -> env=prod-canary, release=console/2026-03-18T11:00Z :rocket:
Jules: I'll own the canary monitor during the window. will watch org_mismatch_count and token-attribution trends.
Sam: creating PR now. patch will change key from `route_prefetch::user:u-42:cookie:...` to `route_prefetch::org:org-9:user:u-42:cookie:...` — also adding migration note in code comments.
Lee: ticket for gateway authoritative fix: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-1242 (assigning to eng-runtime). includes backward compat plan.
Ana: QA: please add a flaky-run label if e2e suspects race timing. we should also run stress tests for 30s org-swap bursts.
qa-bot: added tests -> running once per commit.
Devon: long term we should consider moving prefetch to a per-org cache layer with strict TTLs tied to org session changes. avoids key explosion and is explicit.
Maria: agreed. after canary let's schedule a follow-up retro to decide cadence for gateway change.
Jules: thanks all. will upload logs from canary once live and update the ticket. :pray:
